verdict.rationale: The Department documents a third-party agent role: agents file reemployment tax returns alongside employers and employee leasing companies, and agents add or delete clients through the e-File and e-Pay Enrollment System or a batch file. Nothing in the pack publishes the scope of what an agent may and may not do, an authorization or power-of-attorney form, or which certifications or signatures must stay with the taxpayer; the RT-6 certification screen is not tied to a signer. Missing for 10: published authorization forms, an explicit list of agent permissions and limits, a statement of which signatures or certifications are non-delegable, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: The Department provides employers, agents, and employee leasing companies an application that allows a user to file their reemployment tax return electronically.
Agents must add, delete, or update client information electronically using one of the following methods: Use the e-File and e-Pay Enrollment System
If an agent has 100 or more clients to add or delete, the agent may use a batch enrollment file.
